newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Nov 8.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Nov 8.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Friday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The European Commission has welcomed next week's visit by Deputy President Thabo Mbeki to the EU's executive arm, but Brussels observers say the Pretoria delegation is unlikely to come back home with anything more than sympathy.

- The central Reserve Bank's holding of gold and foreign exchange reserves weathered the storm in the currency markets last month, notching up a surprise 241.5 million rand increase to 10.28 billion rand.
- Banking group Nedcor boosted attributable earnings 38 percent to 1.08 billion rand for the year to September, following a good all-round performance.
- Rainbow Chicken saw its attributable loss increase 100 million rand to 164.4 million for the six months to September as selling prices dropped and feed costs spiralled.
- Portnet executive director Sipho Nyawo was dismissed on Thursday and could face criminal charges relating to credit card abuse.
- Early results from a strike ballot by South Africa's Transport and General Workers' Union show overwhelming support for a strike against members of the Road Freight Employers' Association.

- The value of gold and foreign exchange reserves held by the Reserve Bank rose to 10.28 billion rand last month from 10 billion in September, even after a foreign credit line of 612 million was fully repaid.
- Rainbow Chicken, the ailing broiler group, posted an attributable loss of 164.4 million rand for the six months to September.
- Nedcor, the country's fourth largest bank, enjoyed a rise in net income of 38 percent to more than one billion rand in the year to September.
- The South African Broadcasting Corporation has introduced a new method of collecting licences fees and is bracing itself for the massive confusion the change is likely to cause.
- A high-powered ANC delegation will meet truth commission chairman Archbishop Desmond Tutu on Sunday to resolve persistent wrangles over the amnesty issue.
